title: Videos and Podcasts
subtitle: The Institute's public library of recorded videos and podcasts.
audience: Learners, researchers, and community members who want to watch or listen to Institute sessions, interviews, lectures, and presentations.
lede: Recorded livestreams, learning-group sessions, interviews, lectures, and presentations — published as video on YouTube and as audio on podcast platforms, so anyone can follow the Institute's work as it happens or return to it later. The full, searchable library is below.

sections.heading: What we publish, and why
sections.body: The media library is an open, participatory archive: because sessions are recorded and published rather than held privately, work done live becomes a lasting public resource anyone can watch, sample, or trace across many recordings later. Much of it comes from recurring activities — the Activities page summarizes those rhythms — and it accompanies the Institute's learning pathways, giving newcomers an on-ramp and returning learners a way to revisit harder material at their own pace.

sections.heading: Where to watch and listen
sections.body: The YouTube channel is the authoritative catalogue of recorded sessions; the Podbean feed carries the same library as audio for listening on the go. Both are updated as new sessions are published.
